words.sense: Appearing reasonable but misleading on closer examination
misconceptions: Assuming every false item is specious.
Assuming elegant presentation makes a fake genuine.
Assuming every false item is specious.
Treating an exposed reasoning flaw as proof of forgery.

semantic_axes.description: Specious describes an apparently convincing argument that fails scrutiny; spurious describes something counterfeit or invalid, whether persuasive or not.

edges.boundary_rule: Specious describes an apparently convincing argument that fails scrutiny; spurious describes something counterfeit or invalid, whether persuasive or not.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming every false item is specious.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming elegant presentation makes a fake genuine.
misconceptions.M3: Treating an exposed reasoning flaw as proof of forgery.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amara's argument about the school timetable?

beats.text: Amara says the new timetable suits everyone because all twelve students she asked liked it.
beats.reason: The initial evidence is small sample presented as universal; it best supports specious.

beats.text: She had questioned only pupils who live next to school, though many others travel an hour.
beats.decisive_clue: biased group disguised as universal evidence
beats.reason: The sample never justified a claim about everyone; the added detail exposes its misleading reach.

chains.feedback_short: The sample never justified a claim about everyone; the added detail exposes its misleading reach.
chains.feedback_deep: Specious means superficially persuasive but faulty; spurious means false, invented, or inauthentic. The sample never justified a claim about everyone; the added detail exposes its misleading reach.
chains.contrast_rule: Specious tricks the reasoning; spurious fakes the source.

hints.attention: Look at who the evidence represents.
hints.axis: Specious describes an apparently convincing argument that fails scrutiny; spurious describes something counterfeit or invalid, whether persuasive or not.
hints.contrast: Specious tricks the reasoning; spurious fakes the source.

beats.text: She prints it on thick paper with a gold border.
